I feel like we grew up together in this department, since he was also a beginner when I first took a class from him. He improved his teaching skills, and he makes sure that we all have our resources to follow him. I think he needs to find better ways to keep class interested, especially after the first lecture hour, because sometimes it gets pretty repetitive. I found it hard to follow attentively.
course: If you're interested in Victorian literature/authors, I would recommend it. It feels a bit slow at times, but the readings were enjoyable and the subjects were interesting.

instructor: -Atti is very knowledgeable and is effective at teaching difficult ideas and concepts
He is understanding. He took the difficulty of the material into consideration when grading.

course:

instructor: Dr. Viragh is the best. I genuinely love having conversations with him. He is legit the best at Bilkent.

No one should give this lecture except Atti Viragh, HE IS THE BEST. It was his first time giving this lecture but he was very succesful. The texts he choosed are hard but he is aware of that. I was able to get a lot out of the course because he explained the texts and ideas in as simple a way as possible so that we could understand them. He was always energetic and student friendly. He did his best to help us understand the topics and also used visuals and diagrams. He always taught the lesson with pleasure and I listened to it with pleasure. Thank you hocam.
I think he's a really good person. The course is a difficult and he did everything to make it easier.
course: Although the course is considered the most difficult course in the department, it supports other courses in terms of content.
The course is difficult

instructor: Atti hocadan en son 1. sınıfta ders almıştım ve benim için pek de iyi bir tecrübe olmamıştı. Bu dönem ÇOK daha farklıydı ve dersinden çok keyif aldım. Çok zor textleri bile çok basit ve anlaşılır şekilde anlatıyor, bence bu dersi Atti hocadan daha iyi kimse veremez. Bu ders bana çok şey kattı ve bazı konulardaki bakış açılarımı değiştirdi. Sometimes when you read aloud I find myself having to choose between finding the part in question, so I can highlight it (and thus not really listening), or listening and taking notes, but then having to figure out where it was later on by myself (not always successfully). It'd be nice to be a bit more clear about page counts and paragraphs and such.

He is punctual but his methods should definitely be questioned. He makes it hard for the student to participate in class because he always wants to talk about his ideas and how much better they are. He makes little space for us to contribute and state our ideas. He spends more time defending his own take than really considering our ideas about the subject matter. course: Good selection of texts, I liked that they built off of each other. I appreciated that we covered a variety of topics, too - I liked the animal rights one.
güzel ve keyifli bir ders mi, yoksa atti hoca sayesinde mi keyif aldım? sanırım ikincisi

instructor: Dr. Viragh is a great lecturer. He is always enthusiastic about the course subject and encourages his students to think critically.
I think Dr. Viragh is very good at explaining extremely complex ideas to us as simply as one could do.

He was very knowledgeable about the class material. If you took notes in class, you would not have any struggles, despite the difficulty/uniqueness of the texts. He gave very concise summaries of numerous philosophers and their ideas.
Sometimes it's very difficult to follow his speech. He doesn't use slides for the lecture, which I think might be a problem.
I always enjoy Atti’s classes, he’s been one of my favourite instructors in the department. He’s very knowledgeable and his lectures are always interesting and informative.
He taught us a lesson of how to approach these thinkers which is the biggest favor he could have done to us. He generally showed interest which engaged us more.

Despite the subject, this class didn’t feel very suffocating. The bulk of the material required summaries and explanations through lectures, which were always supplemented by watching videos in class or by group discussions. Dr. Viragh’s responses to participation ranged from strong counterpoints and commentary to silence, but he always ensured he answered questions thoroughly. Overall, I really enjoyed this class; there are always relevant ways to connect lit. theory to culture and society today, and Dr. Viragh made sure to show how. The exams were easy, and the reading material was (initially) quite dense, but I think it all leveled out to a balanced, informative course without high expectations. I would recommend.

Dr. Viragh, though sometimes cutting the students' speech a bit prematurely, always responds thoughtfully and understandingly in a way that usually expands upon or notions or discussions in a natural and effective way, pushing the students to consider new angles.

He was an incredible teaching. The lectures were mostly seminar style so it was hard to participate. I did not appreciate the way the exams were structured. Instead of making it easy, the style made it hard for me to get a good grade even though I studied hard
course: The class was at times too packed. I believe the lit theory course in general can be given gradually over the years. I see 3rd grade as pretty late for taking a theory class.

I think since this is a class with heavy topics with all the theories, it might’ve been easier for us to have some kind of a supplementary material that includes the important concepts. We talk about a lot of different things and sometimes it’s a bit hard to keep up with what’s important for the exam and what isn't.
The assessments were effective in interacting and understanding the material. The material of course is hard so sometimes it was hard to engage.
It was not a discussion based class, but the instructor was clear enough in explaining that further discussion was not necessary to understand class materials.
The course has heavy reading material but it really pays off in the end. It teaches a lot of crucial subjects and changes the way you think about the world.
We learn a lot of essential theories, its a lot, but it still ends up to be  very beneficial.

The readings are, understandably, imbalanced occasionally in terms of how much space and time they take which makes it harder to initially follow certain texts, but the overall course flow is very effective in making connections between distinct theories and schools of thought.
One of the hardest but most crucial courses of the department. I have learned a lot.
assistant: We did not have a TA

instructor: He is very good at explaining theory. He has a very engaging way of lecturing. Sometimes he either gets too excited or a bit confused on how to handle some parts of the theory and somethings are left a bit unclear.
He's the perfect instructor for this course; he was very demanding but encouraging us to learn. As always, I learned so much from him

Atti için önceden “korkutucu” olduğunu duysam da bence gayet nazik ve tatlı bir insan. Ofisine gidip konuşun tanışın çok chill. Derste participation yapmak zor çünkü direkt participation notu yok, onun dışında zorlayan bir insan değil. Özellikle ders anlatış şekline bayılıyorum, zor teoriler işlememize rağmen çok nötr ve anlaşılır bir konudan bahsederek başlayıp, mantıklı relationlar kurup kafanıza ampul yaktırıyor. Dinlediğiniz ve önemli noktaları not aldığınız takdirde sınavlarında zorlanma imkanınız yok, amacı sizi tricklemek değik, gerçekten ilgili öğrenciyi ayırt ediyor.

One of his strengths as a professor is that he makes it easier for students and makes sure that we are not intimidated by any of the material, and connects with us with so much empathy and consideration. He understands what it is like to be a student and does not make us feel inadequate in any way, and answers our questions/participation with so much curiosity and respect. He makes sure that each student is motivated by uplifting us and by pointing out our strengths in a meaningful way.

Academically I have to say that his lectures flow seamlessly and they are very well structured from the beginning to the end. He explains concepts very clearly and in a straightforward manner, not complicating anything and focusing on the sole purpose of teaching the material. He is also an extremely insightful and eloquent speaker.

Another strength is that he has so much humility and finds something respectable and enlightening about each theorist that we read. This is very hard to find in some circles, in my opinion, and it is such a reassuring experience to encounter a professor so open to a spectrum of so many ideas, theories, and ways of looking at/understanding the world! 

Because of these qualities, I feel that I learned an incredible amount from this course and from him, and any student taking his class would benefit greatly from his teaching. He is the best instructor that I have ever taken a course from, and I think that we are lucky to have him as a teacher.
course: Scopeu açısından zor bir ders ama zamanında çalışırsanız ve not alırsanız böyle dikiş dikiyor gibi ilmek ilmek ilerleyerek işi ççözersiniz. Atti zaten zorlayan bir hoca değil, sadece dersi takip edebilin. Gerçekten bayıldığım bir ders oldu. Çok şey öğrendik, her şeyi biraz biraz çalıştık, sadece teorileri spesifik olarak öğrenmedik, bir teori nasıl anlaşılır bunu öğrendik thanks to Atti
might be controversial but i dont think the exams should be multiple choice :(
Great course.

instructor: In a creative project, he mostly uses the excuse of the work being too shallow to force us to change the course of all the events that are happening (or the main arguments) which makes it impossible for us to create a project that is unique to us. Or the point we are trying to make becomes impossible.

There are no weak points. Dr. Viragh gives invaluable feedback about your paper and makes sure to send it to you as early as he can so that you can work on your writing. He always makes time to talk to you in his office about whatever concern you may have. I learned a lot from him and his feedback and can say with certainty that as long as you take his comments into consideration as you’re writing your paper, you will end up with a well-written essay. You just have to put a lot of work and time into your paper.

He is extremely hard to work with. He has his own opinions about a subject and never gives up on the way he thinks one thing should be done. While having him as an advisor for my senior project, I struggled heavily to make him like what I am doing. I do not think he understands that although he is an instructor with great knowledge, we as the seniors are not fish out of the water and somewhat know what we are doing. I do not think he has the perfect approach towards the student to completely discuss certain elements of their work and what they should change. he uses an approach that this strict and not interpretable.
Yok. Atti hoca harika biri. Çok iyi yönlendiriyor ve çok anlayışlı. Sadece biraz ketum. Tam bir profesyonel yani. Makara yapamazsınız pek.

Dr Viragh is probably the best instructor in the department. He is really understanding, helpful and kind. He cares about your work and progress throughout the semester. During our meetings, he guided and helped me a lot to develop my senior project. He also made Modernism really interesting and fun for me. It was one of the best things to work with him. He is so professional and helpful, and he reflects this in his works and his students. I really advise other students to work with him too if possible. I wish I could take more courses that he teaches.
course: The only weak aspect of the course is the deadlines. The final submission is way too early than most of the departments in Bilkent. I understand that the instructors have limited time to read and evaluate the finals, but the final submission for the senior project overlapped with some of our second midterms. It caused a little rush and stress for all of us. Apart from this, generally, it was nice to work on something I love and have interest.
Yok

instructor: He criticizes you and your work a lot but can’t handle when you criticize his views.
course: I think the organization of deadlines for the course could be formatted on a more individual basis. For example, instead of the annotated bibliography being submitted first for the Academic Paper option, close readings or explanatory/research notes could be submitted as requested by individual advisors. I found this specific deadline and its requirements were more of a hindrance than a helpful tool for my project as I needed to complete my close readings and exploration of texts before moving forward with secondary research. Having to find a set number of secondary sources before even beginning writing only made the process harder to manage.
Still, the project thought me a lot on creative writing.

instructor: I feel very lucky to have the opportunity to be supervised by him, and I have learned a lot from this experience. He showed great interest in my project and supported and encouraged me throughout.
He gives great extensive feedback. If you want to take this senior project seriously, he will give as much guidance as possible.
course: I think the deadlines must be clear with dates from the start of the semester. There was a lot of confusion among students and instructors because all the deadlines were listed as end of week 7, end of week 9. A document with all the deadlines listed clearly with dates and times would solve this very easily.

The weakest aspect of the course has nothing to do with Professor Viragh, but I wish the course coordinator were someone else. The deadlines and the way requirements were communicated to students were handled so poorly that they were the hardest part of the senior project.
assistant: the course coordinator should be changed

instructor: He literally only sits in his chair while giving lectures and talks about his own interests. He thinks only his own opinions about the readings are right and does not let you participate. He also blamed students and called us "cheaters" in a very disrespectful tone because he couldn't check his colleagues' syllabus and see that the poem he asked us to close read in his exam has been taught in another course (for multiple semesters too, its not even hard to notice this) not only that but he wasn't even in the exam room at that time so we could ask about it during the exam. Overall he is disrespectful as well as shallow and boring.
No comments

I think he's really interested in what he teaches, and he is open to learn more and more about it rather than claiming his knowledge as ultimate truth. I know that this might be bare minimum but I'm very glad that he opens a space for our own opinions as well without feeling us being judged. / I really believe that checking and asking to colleagues beforehand if a material that he wanted to use in midterms is whether teached or lectured before is his responsibility and we shouldn't be labelled as "cheaters" for picking a thing that we're familiar with. however, I got his point as well so I don't really consider this as negative.
Hocamız gerçekten deneyimli ve ne anlattığına hakim, yalnızca bazen ders sanki tek taraflıymış gibi oluyor

I think he failed to create an atmosphere that allows students to voice their own interpretations of the texts. Most of the time, the classes were about his interpretations and his thoughts. Even when students spoke, he didn't comment or deepen the argument. Usually, he just listens and then continues speaking from where he left off. Additionally, from this class I learned nothing about poetry. I was hoping to get a good idea about the form of poetry and its tools. But he didn't spend any time on them. And even though now I have a term of poetry class, I don't think I can speak confidently about any formal elements because I was not taught about them.  Lastly, I think, he speaks in a way that makes it clear that he doesn't really think your ideas are important because you are a student and he has a PhD. The way he speaks is very belittling.

I think that he is very professional, and even though he is giving the Poetry and Poetics class for the first time, I liked his way of teaching.  However, he is kind of scary. I believe that he has to work on that.
Eloquently spoken, great lecturing skills, not one downside comes to mind.

Most of the classes he gives us long papers to discuss in the class. We spend over 20 minutes to talk nothing afterwards. Needless to say we had already a thick coursepack. He didn't prepare any slides for this course he just sat in his chair. Such an important course should have been teached by another well-prepared instructor.
dersi zevkle anlatması ilgi uyandırıyor fakat sınavda yapılan bir hata hakkında sınıfa attığı mail alay edici bir üsluptaydı. öğrencilere yaklaşımı pek hoş değildi
course: Dersin olumlu tarafları bize birçok şairi ve temalarını ana hatlarıyla tanıtıyor olması ama daha az şair işleyip daha derinlemesine işlememizi yeğlerdim.
Not interesting

Ders Elit 139 dersi ile birkaç küçük ortak alanı bulunduruyordu, daha soyut konuları seven insanlar kesin bu dersi de sevecektim ama şiirler ile alakası olmayan birinin hiç almak istemeyeceği zorunlu bir ders

The course seems out of the general narrative of the ELIT curriculum; poetics could be acknowledged in our first year and not be presented in the third semester. Also, more lecture hours would be appreciated because of how little time there is to cover. There were times that I felt the need to participate, naturally, but also recognised how our instructor had to go over subjects in order to complete them in time, so I held back, and some other peers have thought the same way. Mind you, class participation takes 20 percent of the whole grade.
The syllabus is too complicated and doesn't have a clear timeline or concepts. Or even if it does, the proffesor failed to teach them effectively.
poetry is hard / but I've enjoyed it very much.

I learned almost nothing about poetry and meter because he only does close readings in this class which we are already familiar with from our literature in its contexts and appreciation of literature courses. This course should've been about poetry and poetics not a "What Mr. Viragh thinks about this certain poem!" Course.

instructor: He does not look at his students when he is talking, and he sometimes interrupts people. Apart from that, if you go to his office to ask something he is very helpful and kind.

he is very knowledgeable, always comes to class prepared, teaches every subject very elaboratively and it is clear he is passionate about literature. im glad i took this class and learned a lot from him. its just i hoped he would be a bit more clear on the instructions of assignments but yeah i would say he does not really have weak points.

It often feels as though the class is treated more like middle schoolers than undergraduates. Namely: introducing lexically complex works only to then question if we understand an elementary word like "crawl." This lack of expectation is somewhat insulting and unbecoming. Perhaps he would benefit from trying to engage with students on a more equal intellectual footing. There is a reason few can effectively teach close reading... He is an ordinary instructor who just happens to be rather committed to his own critical readings. This otherwise harmless habit of his renders the entire course ineffectual, given the inherently subjective nature of poetry.
he beefs with students in their 20s and calls it a day. kinda sassy. love him tho.

It was a delightful class, and Professor Viragh is clearly passionate about poetry, in addition to being an efficient instructor. As someone who enjoys poetry, this class has helped me understand and appreciate it a lot more.
course: I disliked the selection and grouping of poets.
love the course.

instructor: i appreciate how he changed himself and his attitude towards us. he is very helpful, guiding and efficient in his topics. love him.

Professor Viragh is very punctual, has an approach to teaching which makes the difficult topics more bearable and interesting, the exams are nothing absurd, it is clear he is simply testing the students critical thinking skills and the knowledge taught in the course.

I think he is kind and considerate in his interactions with students. He puts considerable effort into his lectures and it shows how much he enjoys talking about this subject. One thing that makes the class harder is that he sometimes speaks way too fast when he is lecturing. He does not have any extra notes or material we can look at so we have to take notes constantly in class, which is understandable normally. However, sometimes it becomes really hard to follow because he talks really fast or sometimes in circles. Me and my friends combined our notes to study before the exam but everyone might not have the same opportunity. Overally, he is fair and his classes are very intellectually engaging.
One of the best lecturers in the department.

I like Atti hocam. He is a student-friendly instructor with a great sense of humour, and he is kind, as well as helpful. He is also understanding and respectful, as well as supportive. He is sometimes harsh with the grades and the feedback, but overall, he is quite nice.

For this class particularly, I think the lectures were a bit hard to follow since we didn't have any slides or lecture notes to have as a reference. I had a hard time trying to figure out which of the concepts he talked about were significant and which ones were not. We did lots of theory so I would’ve appreciated if there was a more structured lesson plan of some kind.

Atti is a great professor. He is very organized, disciplined and good at evoking interest. His choosing of texts are interesting. I always liked his syllabus. I think he is the best instructor in the department. We are really lucky to take courses from him. I dont think he has any weak points but he could talk a bit louder maybe.

He is a highly qualified instructor. The course content was well chosen and explored in depth. He also managed to explain and connect various concepts in affect theory to the texts. I am sure that all of the students took something new from the course that will benefit them throughout their bachelor’s studies and beyond. His grading is fair and transparent as well. Overall, it is a great course taught by an excellent instructor.

He’s a perfectionist, but when you do things perfectly, he gives you what you deserve. And if he sees your effort, you can witness his softer side. He is good person and good professor. I do not think that he is so harsh. Please. He deserves better evaluation.
Çok bilgili ancak bazen bizim seviyemizin üzerinde ders anlatıyor.

The strongest points: everything. I felt fortunate to be taking his class, and I believe every student can benefit greatly from his teaching. Initially, when the course first began, I had some worries about some of the material being a bit difficult, but Dr Atti made it easier to understand for all of us while not underestimating the theories or diluting them. His teaching is straightforward and easy to follow; his selections in the syllabus are very thought-provoking (honestly, and after learning them you leave the class changed for the better); and most importantly, he believes that students are capable of working with such complex topics. He is kind, approachable, and thoughtful in engaging with our ideas. weakest points: could not think of one
I always learn a lot from Professor Viragh’s classes. Definitely a high effort class but in my opinion it’s so worth the effort.

He is a great instructor and I think he has improved himself as well since the first year. If you pay attention to the class and I mean, constantly listening and reading the materials, his exams are not hard. He asks what he tells in the class which are things you wouldn't get from the sources on the internet and it wouldn't help much either. He sometimes gets carried away and it feels like he is talking to himself rather than lecturing the class so you need to pay attention whatever he says. Other than that, he is nice and helpful as long as you are engaged with the class.

I think he's a qualified and intellectual instructor. I like his way of teaching because it attracts attention. The only problem related to the course was the overall readings of the course, it was not tough but the readings were too specific for undergraduate students, and too directed to the psychoanalysis
He is a great teacher. Although some texts and concepts were hard to understand, he did his best to make them easier for us. No weak points at all

Dr. Viragh is great, is able to teach difficult topics with as much clarity as possible. However because of the density I believe, he went over somethings really fast and I do understand that we are not supposed to understand everything fully, but still because little parts lead to others when it comes to theory, it was sometimes hard to follow. Maybe focusing on a smaller part of the theory for every week would be more efficient.
I think Dr. Viragh is very passionate about the subjects he’s teaching so his lectures are always interesting. His lectures also make complicated texts much easier to understand.
course: It explorles different concepts compared to other ELIT courses, which is experimental and in depth.
A difficult class that is quite high effort but very enjoyable and you learn so much.
No negative sides

The course was honestly hard. Even harder than ELIT 392. You really get into the theoretical side of the literature which is hard to understand and use it on your own. But it was fun and interesting. There is really a lot to learn.
There were too many texts

This class is INCREDIBLY theory based, for anyone considering to take this course. Be prepared to listen to very long lectures and take notes. The material itself is very interesting though. I learned a lot even if it was a little tedious.
Ders materyalileri çok zor ama çok şey öğrendim.
The lectures helped enlighten the complicated texts we were assigned to read. Also, watching films and using theory to illuminate them both made the films and the theories much more meaningful.
It was almost the best course in our department

The readings were extremely hard as for the language, and the work load is too much. We had too much to read every day, and it was nearly impossible to catch up. But I liked that films were included, since we watched some films within the weeks, and it was a nice break from the extremely heavy amount of theory that we had to deal with pretty much all the time. I also do not really understand why this was not offered as a PSYC course, because this felt within the range of psychology rather than literature.

Perhaps the topics of this course - affect theory - is a bit too specific for an undergrad course. I liked the application of the theories to the films, but maybe leaving out a few less important theorists and instead adding a few literary works (short stories or poems) to apply the theories onto would be better.

instructor: Strongest: effective communication, stimulating interest, explaining complex topics in a way that is easier to understand

he’s very good at making the materials engaging, and giving relevant historical context. really piqued my interest and curiosity
also love the “no AI” policy and how strict he is about it
I think he is passionate about what he teaches and it shows in the classroom. He is a great instructor mainly because of that.

I can't believe I'm typing this: he's too nice. He's a lovely person, beautifully articulate, great at lecturing, very generous, very helpful, constantly doing his absolute best to trigger student interest, empathetic to the student condition... to the point where I was often left thinking that if he were even slightly more mean, slightly tougher on grading, slightly more critical I'd actually get more out of the course. I feel like both himself and his students would benefit from a heavier hand and higher expectations. I might just be insane though. I don't know.

I will say this though: I am not an ELIT major, and from the outside this looks like a departmental problem rather than an Atti problem. I don't think he's the kind of person who inherently dislikes academic rigor. I'm sure the American standard of the student/instructor relationship also plays an inevitable part here.

I can't even criticize him without diverting it. He's too sweet! He has great taste in cinema too. Impossible to dislike.
course: i really loved the texts we did, maybe more optional readings to give more context could be good

Strongest: the reading materials assigned and the range of topics covered

I think there should be mandatory PSYC courses for the ELIT department students. Not limited to this course but for the courses like these, that are heavily based on psychology, one or two PSYC courses would be efficient for analyzing the course material.

instructor: He was the best instructor ever he really made me love the department he was so passionate and so enthusiastic throughout all the lectures he really helped me to understand even the hardest text He was so helpful thoughtful I don’t think I can give any bad comments to such a good teacher
Dr. Atti Viragh communicated well with his students and presented the topics he talked about in an engagingly beautiful way.
course: In terms of the works in the Syllabus, they were all very well thought out and good sources. It is fundamental for us to learn all these things.
Every text we read was so good. The only thing I think is we could analyze wasteland more

instructor: I believe Dr. Viragh is a good fit for the department, and his lecturing is on par with others. His teaching style is clear, his expectations are also clear. It would've been better if he utilized Moodle like the others. And I wish the quizzes were spread evenly throughout the semester instead of the last couple weeks. Apart from these decisions, I enjoyed his teaching and he is really easy to communicate with, which helps.

He is able to draw our interest into the topic he is teaching. However, his relationship with his students is not ideal. The responses he gives sometimes come off as negative or insulting. He forgot he was giving an exam and us students waited for an hour, it was really disrespectful as we were there at 08.30. Some people live far away and this means some of us wake up at 6 to go to the exam which the instructor forgets about. He squeezed all the exams into last two weeks and they were all about the same book. He reads the quiz questions aloud in the first 3 minutes of the quiz so if you are late, a big part of your grade is gone. It does not matter if you are late for the first time ever the whole semester, he does not give the questions again. He only does it for his favorite students.
He is so kind, and his voice is so soothing. It is really a pleasure to attend his classes. He is probably one of the best instructors in ELIT department.
once he forgot the exam. things he taught were enjoyable but he couldn't really stimulate active class discussion

Almost no positive aspect. Unfortunately he was so disorganized and did not clearly what he expected from us. He even forgot face to face midterm even though he warned us "not to get late to the exam". It was ironic. He was so irresponsible and did the quizzes after week 9. Quizzes were also imprecise and I think no one figured out how he evaluated quizzes. To learn what he expects from students you should always go to his office and ask the details yourself. Compared to other instructors in ELIT department, he is so neglectful and reading materials (except Kundera and Woolf) were also dull. He was unable to analyze every single material he put on coursepack. Also, he did not care about what his students think and our contributions to the class had no meaning because it was clear that he was unsatisfied with our answers. He is intellectual and knows too much it is clear but I think his communication skills are bad. He does not even make an eye contact while talking with you or lecturing...

Positive aspect: Most of the works that he chooses for reading were good. Especially The Unbearable Lightness of Being, which is amazing for a literature course to examine whole range of concepts in one book.
Negative aspect: He does not answering e-mails for the writing assignments, he only accepts questions in his office hours, which is hard to follow always since we have other classes as well.
He was unfair in grading presentations. Also, he mistaken the hour of the in-class midterm once, and showed up late and postponed the other section of the exam the following week, which made everything more stressful.

I think Dr. Viragh did a great job at sparking our interests with the subjects he was teaching. He gave many handouts that not only helped with his course but other courses as well. He is passionate and knowledgable at what he is teaching which makes his lessons great.
course: The course requires the ability to thoroughly analyze texts, but Dr. Viragh helped us a lot.
overall, the course is really enjoyable, in fact I have read the best text and books in the course of my studies at Bilkent with this course

instructor: He simply has no respect for his students. The course environment genuinely feels dehumanizing. While this reflects the growing pains many modernist authors have had around the turn of the 20th century, I did not really have to experience instructor induced alienation to talk about it.

He is a great lecturer and an awful everything else. I have no idea how to approach the readings: we have surprise quizzes that ask minute details, followed by two hours of class where he just explains what happened in the assigned readings. He dedicates twenty minutes each class to read a page that we already should have read. If he’s going to summarize the plot and have us take 30 minutes reading a page, then why am I supposed to read the material in advance? If he does not expect us to come having already read, why do the quizzes?? His line of thinking does not hold up unless he believes that students, even after reading the materials, are too stupid to understand what’s going on by themselves. The only interesting moments of this class happened when Atti went outside this hellish approach and introduced to our discussions concepts and contexts that illuminated our readings. I would have loved this class if he had dropped the habit of acting as Sparknotes in each lecture.

First of all, it is true that my attention and interest in literature have awakened because of your passion. However, in classes, I feel like you only discuss topics with the people who actually know about literature. In the first semester too, you did not teach us the course as if we were seeing these topics for the first time in our lives. It was like making someone with no musical talent the head of an orchestra. I did not know anything about English Literature, yet, I could not learn much either. I always felt unwelcome and not enough because everyone seemed to know the topics really well while I did not understand anything. You have actually given a lecture about ''Post-humanism" in class and I understood the topic really well, moreover, it is the only topic I fully understood besides my group project. But for other theories, it was only slides and a few comments on them so I really had difficulty in learning them. The classes felt like we are only gathering for commenting on books, like a book club. As someone who is taking this lecture, English Literature for the first time you have failed to make me understand so many topics. It is my fault too, at some point I could not focus since I did not know anything, to begin with. I wish you could have explained all the theories to us in more detail, and understand that we were taking this class for the first time. The second year is on the way and for my literature knowledge, I still have trouble knowing even the basics.

First of all, I like your passion for literature. You were excited in the classes. In addition, you were really understanding this semester as well. However, you only talked the students who had an idea what we were doing. You don't seem interested in teaching. You just love to talk about literature. You discuss the topics as if we actually knew them and were on the same level as you. We were just coming, commenting on the book and leaving. It is the same as the first semester. You acted like we took any literature lecture before in high school but we didn't. I wasn't interested in literature before so I had an difficulty in understanding. However, I really have been trying to love literature and to learn something. I really haven't learned a thing in two semester and it was really hard for me.
